title: STRAND GUARD for TRA-2820: an issue with an open blockedBy structurally cannot arm a monitor (422 vs 409), so it goes dark the instant its last blocker closes
description:
Filed by CTO 2026-09-16 as the STRAND GUARD for **TRA-2820**, which cannot carry one itself.

## Why this row exists: TRA-2820 is structurally incapable of having a wake path

On 2026-09-16 I tried to arm an issue monitor directly on TRA-2820 and measured a hard catch-22.
Both guards are working as designed; **together** they guarantee the hole:

| attempt | result |
|---|---|
| `PATCH TRA-2820 {executionPolicy.monitor}` while `blocked` | **422** `Monitor can only be scheduled on issues assigned to an agent in in_progress or in_review` |
| `PATCH TRA-2820 {"status":"in_progress"}` to become eligible | **409** `Issue follow-up blocked by unresolved blockers` |

So: an issue resting on an open blocker **may not leave `blocked`**, and a `blocked` issue **may not
arm a monitor**. An issue whose `blockedBy` is non-empty therefore CANNOT hold a scheduled wake, and
when its last blocker closes there is no wake, no auto-flip and no monitor -- it goes dark silently.
That is not an agent forgetting to arm something. It is enforced by the platform's own two guards,
and it is why this shape is visible only to the strand detector (TRA-4580 / TRA-4583).

title: ROOT CAUSE for TRA-2956/TRA-2820: Infinity is used as the tp1 no-take-profit sentinel and JSON.stringify(Infinity)===null, so mark >= tp1Premium becomes mark >= 0 - the sentinel inverts from NEVER to ALWAYS and fires a bogus tp1 25s after every open
description:
**Root cause for [TRA-2956](/TRA/issues/TRA-2956), and it also resolves the open question I left on [TRA-2820](/TRA/issues/TRA-2820). Filed separately only because I handed TRA-2956 to CTO before finishing this analysis and the write boundary locked me out of my own ticket — please fold this into TRA-2956 rather than working it twice.**

Found 2026-08-05T18:5xZ reading the live SHA `7b4cb2fe`. No new prod reads; this is analysis of the same 18:39Z snapshot.

## The one-line version

`Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` is used as the "never take profit" sentinel for `tp1Premium`. **`JSON.stringify(Infinity)` is `null`.** After any serialization round-trip the sentinel is `null`, and the TP1 trigger compares `mark >= opt.tp1Premium` — which for `null` coerces to **`mark >= 0`, true for every positive mark.** The sentinel inverts from *never* to *always*.

## The chain, end to end

`options-account.ts:3530` @ `7b4cb2fe`:

```js
if (!opt.tp1Hit && mark >= opt.tp1Premium && opt.contractsRemaining > 1) {
  const exitContracts = Math.floor(opt.contractsRemaining * partialExitRatio);
  ...
  opt.pendingExit = { qty: exitContracts, limitPrice: opt.tp1Premium, kind: 'tp1', pricing: 'limit', ... }
```

title: Engine-opened live option close: mirror to Tradier + smart limit pricing
description:
## Two remaining gaps under [TRA-351](/TRA/issues/TRA-351) - engine-opened live options leak on Tradier, market orders fill terribly

Parent diagnosis: the dashboard's Current Mark / unrealized P&L for Tradier-imported rows has been fixed in [commit 30a790b](https://github.com/Networkgems/TradingAI-/commit/30a790b) (TRA-351 commit). The two remaining issues both stem from the close path being broker-blind.

### Gap 1 - Engine-opened live option closes don't fire on Tradier

`POST /api/options/:id/close` for a non-imported row at `packages/server/src/index.ts:1430` calls:

```ts
const closed = ctx.engine.manualCloseOption(id);
```

`manualCloseOption` -> `account.closeOption(optionId)` is **paper-only**. It moves the local row to `closedOptions`, credits the paper cash bucket with `mark x contracts x 100`, and broadcasts. No Tradier API call is made.

But in live mode, the OPEN side of the position fired a real `buy_to_open` on Tradier (`signal-engine.ts:1013`, `tradierLiveClient.buyContracts`). So after the user hits Close in TradeAI:
- The local row disappears
- Tradier still holds the long option
- The next `/api/tradier/positions/sync` re-imports it as an unrelated "Tradier" row

title: Options Chain Relative Value Scanner
description:
**Volatility surface / volatility skew mispricing**
More specifically: **strike-skew anomaly**, **implied-volatility outlier**, or **relative-value options mispricing**.

Your idea is not just “cheap call / cheap put.” It is:

> Find options whose price or implied volatility is abnormal compared with nearby strikes in the same expiration chain.

Important terms:
**ITM / ATM / OTM** \= in-the-money, at-the-money, out-of-the-money.
**Moneyness** \= how far the strike is from current stock price.
**Implied volatility / IV** \= the volatility level implied by the option’s market price; higher IV usually means a more expensive option.
**Volatility skew / smile** \= IV normally changes across strikes, so the app should compare each option to a fitted curve, not a flat line.
**No-arbitrage violations** \= hard pricing errors, such as a call trading below intrinsic value.
**Vertical spread check** \= compare neighboring strikes with same expiration/type; calls should generally get cheaper as strike increases, puts should generally get more expensive as strike increases.

title: live-capital-gate: positive_expectancy must grade FAIL when the 2σ upper bound (cluster-robust) is below the bar — UNDERPOWERED only when the interval straddles it (CFO ruling TRA-4734)
description:
**CFO ruling on TRA-4734. Delegated to CTO.** `positive_expectancy` must be able to grade **FAIL** when the confidence interval already sits entirely below the bar. Today `UNDERPOWERED` pre-empts `FAIL` unconditionally (`packages/server/src/live-capital-gate.ts:317-322`), so live bqb1 (`c94a5debce35`) prints "a PASS or FAIL from this sample would be a coin flip" over a book whose upper bound is ~3 SE below the bar.

## The defect
`nRequired = (2σ/δ)²` with δ = 0.03R is a **design-stage** sample size: how many rows it takes to resolve an effect to ±0.03R *when the mean sits near the bar*. It is not a stopping rule. The criterion asks one one-sided question: is E[netR] > 0.10? When the mean is far from the bar, that question is answered long before n_req. The code comment's premise ("a FAIL here would assert the book underperformed a bar it could have cleared, on a sample that resolves nothing") is false whenever the interval excludes the bar.

## Required rule (asymmetric; do not loosen PASS)
Precedence stays `INFEASIBLE` > everything else. Below that:

- **FAIL**: `mean + 2·SE_eff < barR`, **and** `n ≥ minResolvedIdeas` (30), **and** weeks ≥ `minWeeksWithResolved` (8).

Price-space isotonic repair. Within each (expiration, optionType) bucket of a response's surviving candidates, sorted by strike, project the raw theo sequence onto the nearest monotone sequence (PAVA, pool-adjacent-violators, unweighted L2): calls non-increasing in strike, puts non-decreasing. title: Implement warning banner and exposure indicators when viewMode=demo on live-armed account
description:
## Context

TRA-4284 identified that when an operator account has `mode="live"` but `viewMode="demo"` persisted, the dashboard shows the demo book (empty) while real money rows sit hidden in the live book. The TRA-3910 chip shows "Viewing DEMO book . engine is LIVE" but doesn't indicate exposure in the hidden book.

## Requirements

1. **Expose hidden book status**: When `viewMode=demo` on a `mode=live` account, the dashboard must show:
   - Count of open live rows in the hidden book
   - Whether any are breached
   - Whether any are inert/unactionable

2. **Escalate breaches to banner**: If the hidden live book has `breached > 0`, this must appear as a banner (alongside `HaltBanner` / `LiveCredentialsBanner`), not just a chip. An operator must not be able to miss this.

3. **Persistence decision**: Decide and document whether `viewMode: demo` should persist across sessions on a live-armed operator account. Document the decision and rationale.

4. **Preserve the feature**: Do NOT fix this by removing the view override. It's a legitimate feature; the defect is that it's silent about what it hides.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A view override on a live account surfaces the hidden book

Routine execution leaves **always** inherit the routine's `assigneeAgentId` — **830 of 830, zero create-time mis-routes**, classifier reachability controlled in both directions. title: The NYSE calendar ends at 2026: first miss is 2027-01-01, and it mis-dates every per-ET-day fold, not just the session gate
description:
<!-- deploy-order: none -->

## Verified

`packages/server/src/scheduler.ts:19` — `MARKET_HOLIDAYS` is a hard-coded `Set` holding **2025 and 2026
only**. There are **zero `2027-` dates anywhere in non-test server source**. `isMarketDay` (`:82`) falls
through to a weekday check, so from 2027 every holiday is treated as a **market day**.

**First miss: 2027-01-01** (a Friday) — ~114 days out. Early closes are not modelled at all.

Trading on a closed day mostly gets refused by the broker. The quieter damage is to **evidence**: the same

`an-et-day-fold-compares-two-builds-across-a-deploy` for how a bad day key manufactures verdicts). A
promotion decision computed off a mis-dated fold looks completely ordinary.

title: TRA-3927.6 OTM sleeve: profit-lock gives back 100% of the gain that arms it (arm 1.0R == giveback 1.0R)
description:
## Problem

`PROFIT_LOCK_ARM_R` and `PROFIT_LOCK_GIVEBACK_R` are **both 1.0** (`packages/shared/src/index.ts:2277-2278`). The rule arms once peak favourable excursion reaches +1.0R and then exits when open R has retraced 1.0R from that peak (`packages/engine/src/exit-rules.ts:211-213`):

```
armed      = peakR >= 1.0
giveBackR  = peakR >= 2.0 ? 0.5 : 1.0
shouldExit = armed && currentR <= peakR - giveBackR
```

Because the arm threshold and the give-back allowance are the **same number**, the rule's exit floor in its first armed state is **zero profit**. Any winner whose peak lands in `[1.0R, 2.0R)` is released somewhere in `[0.0R, 1.0R)` -- and a winner that peaks just over the arm is released at essentially breakeven. This is arithmetic, not variance.

## Measured live instance -- 2026-08-25

Read this beat off bqb1 `877d8f3a83709a75c4dcfc232640f992a1d971b0` (pid 75, `startedAt 2026-08-25T20:14:48.795Z`), row from `/api/trades/export?markets=options`:

| mode / strategy | `live` / `otm_mispricing` |
| entry_time / entry_price | `2026-08-24T14:44:33.832Z` / `1.51` |
| exit_time / exit_price | `2026-08-25T13:45:23.481Z`

title: Password reset: the code map is keyed by CODE ALONE with no throttle, so brute force runs against every account's outstanding code at once
description:
<!-- deploy-order: none -->

## The amplification the audit missed

The external audit (H4) correctly lists: `auth.ts:218` generates the reset code with
`Math.floor(10_000_000 + Math.random() * 90_000_000)` — **`Math.random`, not a CSPRNG** — stored **plaintext**
in `reset-tokens.json`, and asks for throttling. What it does not say is why the combination is worse than it
looks:

- `auth.ts:192` keys the outstanding-reset map by **the code alone** — `resetTokens.get(code)` — **not** by
  username+code.
- There is **no rate limiter of any kind on the auth routes**, including `POST /api/auth/reset-password`.

So a brute-force run is not against one account's 8-digit code. It is against the **union of every outstanding
code across all ~67 accounts**, with unlimited attempts. An attacker who fires `forgot-password` at many
usernames shrinks the search space proportionally and then guesses into the whole pool at once. That makes
this a plausible **account-takeover** path rather than hardening — and it makes the **throttle** the first
fix, ahead of the CSPRNG.

## Work, in this order

1. **Throttle + attempt cap** on `/api/auth/reset-password` and `/api/auth/forgot-password` (per-IP and

title: Confirm Tradier's actual submit/cancel semantics in sandbox, and prove one economic order per intent end to end
description:

Split out of TRA-4476. That ticket's Validation section says broker-specific semantics "need confirming against current Tradier docs + sandbox — **do not assume**". TRA-4476 honoured that by building a reconcile that is correct WITHOUT any broker cooperation. This ticket does the confirming.

## Why the shipped code deliberately assumes nothing

TRA-4476 sends **nothing new to the broker**. No `tag`, no client id, no changed body. That was a deliberate refusal: adding an unverified parameter to an order body on a path where `liveEquityTradingEnabled: true` risks a broker rejection of real orders to buy a nicety. The reconcile therefore keys on `account × bounded time window × class/side/symbol/optionSymbol/quantity`, which needs no broker feature.

The cost of that choice, stated: two economically identical orders in the same window are indistinguishable, and resolve to `unresolved: multiple_matches` — a halt, which is the safe direction but a false one.

description:
The strand DRAIN exits 2 FAILED whenever an origin routine's TITLE contains a non-ASCII character. Measured on the CFO arm fire of 2026-08-27 (TRA-4128, run eb5691e8-ec75-4514-8926-b6dff981a21a), checkout at 8ff3c6a, drainer at b4f5e302.

`originSentence()` (scripts/drain-blocked-empty.mjs) interpolates the origin routine's title VERBATIM into the SUPPRESSING LEAF audit comment:

    Origin routine `${id}` = "${origin.title || '(untitled)'}", status ...

`gradeWriteBody(step='comment')` then grades that same body ASCII-only:

    const nonAscii = body.body.match(/[^\x20-\x7E

\t]/g);
